transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Redwood CSM); Dana Liu (MorrowPoint Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Platform Eng), Evelyn Cruz (Security), Omar Benitez (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick activation / ops handoff for MorrowPoint's pilot. Focus areas: VPC/networking intake, private vs dedicated tradeoffs, pilot performance plan, security artifacts (SOC2/KMS/data residency), and runbook ownership. Agreed to a short pilot for inference throughput tests on Redwood Dedicated with fallbacks to hosted API.

Topics covered:
- VPC peering & staging access flow
- Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API for latency-sensitive scoring
- Pilot benchmarking: dataset size, sequence lengths, concurrency targets
- Security: KMS, audit logs, retention windows, SSO/SAML mapping
- Rollout playbook and who owns which runbook steps

Action items (recorded on call): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex M: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE on the account, Samir is our systems eng, Janelle helps with onboarding. how's everyone doing?
[00:16] Dana: good thanks, uh a bit rushed today but excited to get moving.
[00:22] Alex M: Great. goal for today is to hand off ops, confirm the pilot scope, and make sure security and networking are lined up so Samir can run the perf tests next week.
[00:34] Marcus: yeah we want to validate tail latency under our production-ish load. typical seq lengths are, like, 128 to 512 tokens depending on context. throughput target is around 1200 rps across the pool, but first step is a smaller smoke test.
[00:53] Samir: cool — that helps. just to clarify, when you say 1200 rps is that per region or global?
[01:02] Marcus: that's global target — most traffic will be NA-east though, we do have EU customers so a small % will land there.
[01:11] Samir: got it. for the pilot we'd recommend Dedicated pool in NA-east so we can reserve GPUs and replicate your concurrency. we can also show a hosted fallback route if capacity spikes. note: the dedicated option gives predictable KV cache behavior and steady latency, the hosted tends to have more variance but is faster to start.
[01:33] Dana: can you explain the K V cash stuff again? sorry my notes transcribed that weirdly earlier.
[01:40] Samir: yeah K V cash — the KV cache: for chat-style workloads we keep key-value cache in memory to avoid recomputing prefixes which improves per-token latency. for long sequences your cache hit-rate changes, so we'll instrument that in the benchmark.
[01:53] Alex M: and we'll surface token-level cost breakdowns in the console so you can see where batching and caching are saving you money.
[02:01] Evelyn: quick security question — do you support customer-managed K M S? we need to know if keys can live in our HSM.
[02:08] Samir: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we integrate with common KMS providers; in-hosted mode we maintain encryption at rest but we can tie into your KMS via a connector in the V P C option.
[02:23] Evelyn: okay, also we need the SOC two and ISO summaries — a short bullet doc so legal can pre-check.
[02:29] Janelle: we'll attach the SOC2 summary and ISO cheat sheet. Alex will follow up.
[02:34] Alex M: yes sending those after call.
[02:36] 
[02:40] Marcus: on network — we prefer AWS Transit VPC peering, we'll provide a staging VPC. what do you need from us to grant access?
[02:48] Samir: we need the peering CIDR blocks, list of NAT gateways, and a small allowlist for the staging cluster's control plane. we'll put a checklist in the runbook.
[03:01] Marcus: good. Omar will be our point for that.
[03:05] Omar: yep cool, will send the VPC details by tomorrow.
[03:09] Samir: perfect. from there Samir: sorry — from there Samir will schedule a two hour pilot window, we'll run the benchmark script, gather latency p95/p99, per-token cost, and KV cache hit-rate.
[03:21] Dana: what's the plan if we hit a regression vs our current baseline? I mean, we have a few experiments stacked in prod already.
[03:30] Alex M: good question. we run a quality regression check using your eval set; if model-level quality drops beyond threshold we have canary rollback and automatic fallback routing to a compatible model variant — it's in the rollout playbook.
[03:44] Dana: okay, and how do we pin to a model version during the pilot? we don't want production drift.
[03:49] Samir: you can pin model version in config — we'll map the config to the Dedicated pool. for hosted fallback we recommend a compatible quantized variant but you can pin strictly if you want no surprises.
[04:02] Marcus: about cost — do you have a public worksheet? we want to model monthly committed spend if we go dedicated.
[04:10] Alex M: yes, I'll share a Dedicated pricing worksheet — it has examples for different commit levels plus expected unit costs after batching and cache savings.
[04:19] Dana: anything on SSO? we use Okta and want SCIM for team provisioning.
[04:25] Janelle: we support SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning for user sync. we'll need a SAML metadata file from your side, Alex will get the template to you.
[04:35] Evelyn: audit logs — are they per-tenant and exportable to our SIEM?
[04:41] Samir: yes, audit logs are tenant-scoped and we can stream to your cloudwatch or a syslog endpoint; also we offer log retention options as part of the Private plan.
[04:52] Dana: on the pilot dataset — we'll provide a sampled corpus representative of 10k requests with varying seq lengths. is that enough?
[05:00] Samir: yes that's a good start. ideally include worst-case prompts for the p99 measurement.
[05:06] Marcus: timeline wise — we want this pilot done before the end of quarter. is that feasible?
[05:13] Alex M: absolutely, we can do the benchmark next week, iterate, then you get results and we align on Dedicated commit discussion before quarter end.
[05:22] 
[05:25] Speaker 1: (mumble) also, are there any known issues with long context for your runtime? like extended sequences more than 2k?
[05:34] Samir: our runtime supports optimized attention for long contexts; we recommend quant profiles for longer sequences and may need to adjust kernel selection — we'll note that for the pilot. sometimes, the conv engine will pick a different kernel which can affect perf, so we'll capture that detail in the benchmark report.
[05:53] Dana: who on Redwood side is leading the runbook updates?
[05:57] Janelle: I'll own the runbook drafts and Alex will review; Samir will own the benchmark artifacts.
[06:05] Marcus: ok last question — any blockers on our side to get started right away?
[06:10] Alex M: only the VPC peering details and staging creds from Omar, and Evelyn's confirmation on KMS scope. once we have those we can schedule the 2-hour window.
[06:20] Omar: I'll send the VPC info tonight, expect a mail from me.
[06:24] Evelyn: legal will want the SOC2 doc — Janelle said you'd attach that?
[06:29] Janelle: yep attaching after call.
[06:31] 
[06:34] Recap and next steps:
- Alex to send onboarding runbook, pricing worksheet, SOC2/ISO summary and SAML template (by 2026-12-15).
- Marcus/Omar to provide VPC peering details and staging creds (by 2026-12-16).
- Samir to prepare pilot benchmark script and schedule a 2hr run (pilot window target 2026-12-17 to 2026-12-21).
- Evelyn to confirm KMS/HSM scope and retention constraints (by 2026-12-18).

End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mislabels (Speaker 1) and imperfect word recognition (K V cash = KV cache; Redwood Privet = Redwood Private).
